You are researching Confluence documentation for the "Zimmermann PWA Kit" project — a production Salesforce Commerce Cloud PWA Kit storefront for the Australian fashion brand Zimmermann (repo: zimmermann-pwa). Your job is a READ-ONLY deep dive into Confluence, not the local repo, to produce a report for a Frontend Development Lead who just joined the project (first time on this codebase) and needs to know what to read, review, and set up per Confluence's prescriptions.

## What you already know going in
The repo's AGENTS.md footer names a Confluence space with at least these pages (URLs use base `https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/`):
- "Claude Code CLI — Developer Onboarding Guide" — spaces/SFCC/pages/304775192 (session checklist, prompting guide)
- "1.2 Team Overview" — spaces/SFCC/pages/261586947 (contacts)
- "Claude Code Skills Reference" — spaces/SFCC/pages/297959425 (useful skills)

Also, a repo skill (`.claude/skills/project-init`) references a Confluence page called "7.1c CI/CD & Environment Setup Checklist" that it updates as setup items are confirmed — this strongly implies a numbered page hierarchy (e.g. 1., 1.1, 1.2 ... 7., 7.1, 7.1a/b/c...) with many more sections than just the three pages named above. Your job is to find that full structure, not just the three known pages.

## What to do
1. Use the Confluence MCP tools (confluence_search, confluence_get_page, confluence_get_space_page_tree, confluence_get_page_children, confluence_get_labels, confluence_get_page_history as needed) to:
   a. Fetch the three known pages above in full (not just titles) to confirm the space key (likely "SFCC") and understand the numbering convention.
   b. Pull the full page tree for that space (confluence_get_space_page_tree, or walk confluence_get_page_children recursively from the space root) to see ALL pages, not just the ones already linked from the repo.
   c. Search (confluence_search) for keywords like: "React", "PWA Kit", "onboarding", "setup", "environment", "checklist", "architecture", "coding standards", "git", "workflow", "frontend", "component", "Storybook", "testing", "Playwright", "design system", "Figma", "Contentful", "sprint", "release", to catch anything the page-tree walk might miss (e.g. pages in a different space, or unlinked pages).
   d. For every page that looks relevant to a REACT/FRONTEND DEVELOPER specifically (not e.g. a backend/SFCC-admin-only or pure business/marketing page), open and actually read the full page body — don't just note the title. Prioritize: developer onboarding / session checklist, environment & tooling setup (accounts, access, local env, secrets), coding standards / conventions, architecture overview, git/branching workflow, testing conventions, design system / Figma / Storybook, CI/CD & environment setup checklist (the "7.1c" page and its siblings), team/contacts overview, and the Claude Code skills reference.
   e. Note the full numbered hierarchy you find (e.g. "1. Overview / 1.1 ... / 1.2 Team Overview / 2. ... / 7. Setup / 7.1 ... / 7.1c CI/CD & Environment Setup Checklist") so I can see what other numbered sections exist even if you didn't fully read every single one — flag any you skipped due to low relevance to a React developer (e.g. finance, legal, backend-only ops) so I know they were seen but intentionally deprioritized.

2. Do NOT modify anything in Confluence (no create/update/delete/comment) — this is read-only research.

## What to report back (this is what matters most)
Produce a structured report with:
- **The full page tree/hierarchy you found**, with page titles, IDs/links, and one-line description of each, organized by section number if a numbering convention exists.
- **A prioritized "must read/review" list specifically for a React developer** — pull out concrete content, not just page names: e.g. exact setup steps prescribed (tool installs, account access needed, env var setup, repo access, VPN/SSO, IDE config, Figma/Contentful/BrowserStack/Jira-Confluence access, etc.), concrete coding conventions or architecture notes mentioned, and anything that duplicates or conflicts with what's already in the repo's AGENTS.md/.claude/rules (flag conflicts explicitly, don't just silently note them).
- **A "setup checklist" section** — every concrete, actionable setup step prescribed anywhere in Confluence (accounts to request, tools to install, credentials/tokens to obtain, access to request and from whom), in the order Confluence suggests doing them, noting which ones are mechanical/automatable vs. require a human (e.g. "ask X for access to Y").
- **Anything Confluence says that the repo docs don't already cover** (this is the most valuable part — don't just restate AGENTS.md).

Keep the report thorough but organized — use headers and bullet lists. This report will be relayed directly to the user, so make it complete enough to stand alone, but don't pad it with content that isn't actually in Confluence (e.g. don't restate generic React best practices — only report what these specific Confluence pages actually say).

## 4. Conflicts & Gaps vs. Repo Docs (the most valuable part)

### Direct conflicts — flag to the team, don't silently pick one

1. **Icons — direct contradiction.** AGENTS.md (Rules → Icons): *"Use `overrides/app/components/icons` — this is the single source of truth... Do not import from `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/icons` directly."* Confluence's **[Development Standards](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/261750785)** page says the opposite: *"For icons, use `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/icons`. If a required icon is missing, get it from Figma or ask the UI Designer."* This is Confluence documenting the **older/pre-override** pattern. AGENTS.md is almost certainly the current source of truth (it's Tier 1, actively maintained), but per the doc-integrity rule this should be raised so Confluence gets corrected rather than left contradicting the repo.

2. **New-component folder location — discrepancy.** Confluence's **[Component Override Strategy](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/261881857)** says brand-new Zimmermann components (no base equivalent) go under `overrides/app/components/custom/<name>/` (e.g. `overrides/app/components/custom/backInStockButton/`). The repo's `.claude/rules/conventions.md` (File naming and folder structure) makes no mention of a `custom/` subfolder — it describes every component living directly under `overrides/app/components/<name>/`, and the repo's own `/new-component` skill and worked example in the Onboarding Guide (`overrides/app/components/backInStockButton/index.tsx`) also skip the `custom/` layer. Worth confirming with the team which is current — this looks like Confluence describing an earlier plan that didn't make it into the actual repo convention.
